question: When Walter drove up to the gasoline pump, he noticed that his gasoline tank was \(\dfrac18\) full. He purchased \(7.5\) gallons of gasoline for \(\$10.\) With this additional gasoline, his gasoline tank was then \(\dfrac58\) full. The number of gallons of gasoline his tank holds when it is full is
solution:
The purchased gasoline accounts for the increase in the fraction of the tank that is full:
\[
\frac58-\frac18=\frac48=\frac12.
\]
Thus \(7.5\) gallons fill half the tank. The full tank holds twice that amount:
\[
7.5\div\frac12=7.5\cdot2=15.
\]
The capacity is \(15\) gallons, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
